svg.aria-label: Cost-curve diagram, shape only, not measured data. X axis is stack depth from 1 to about 1100 frames; y axis is nanoseconds to construct, throw and catch, labelled as shape not measured. Three lines: a normal exception rises roughly linearly with depth because Throwable's constructor calls fillInStackTrace, which walks every frame, until a vertical red dashed line marks the measured default of -XX:MaxJavaStackTraceDepth at 1024, past which the walk stops and the line goes flat. A stackless exception, built with the four-argument Throwable constructor with writableStackTrace false or by overriding fillInStackTrace to return this, is drawn flat and low across the whole range. A boolean return is drawn as a flat baseline near zero. A marked point partway along the normal curve is called out as the moment getStackTrace or printStackTrace is invoked, when the compact backtrace object is lazily decoded into a StackTraceElement array, a second cost paid only on that call. Annotation panels state that -XX:-StackTraceInThrowable is the JVM-wide off switch with measured default true, and that the case that matters is the insufficient-funds path at 1,200 stake reservations per second, where InsufficientFundsException is thrown as an expected business outcome on the hot path — exactly where a stackless exception earns its keep.

x = stack depth (frames). MaxJavaStackTraceDepth measured default: 1024 (intx, product) — the walk stops and the curve flattens past this line.
-XX:-StackTraceInThrowable
JVM-wide off switch for fillInStackTrace; measured default on this build: true — the walk runs unless explicitly disabled.
The same flat shape is reached another way: override fillInStackTrace() to "return this" without calling the native walk.
THE CASE THAT MATTERS
InsufficientFundsException thrown as an expected business outcome on the hot path — the insufficient-funds path at
1,200 stake reservations/sec. This is exactly where a stackless exception (the flat curve above) earns its keep.
Four-arg ctor: Throwable(String message, Throwable cause, boolean enableSuppression, boolean writableStackTrace=false).
LEGEND
normal exception — rises ~linearly with depth (fillInStackTrace walks every frame); shape, not measured data
stackless exception — flat, independent of depth (4-arg ctor with writableStackTrace=false, or fillInStackTrace()→this)
boolean return — flat baseline near zero, drawn for comparison only
MaxJavaStackTraceDepth cap — measured default 1024; walk stops and the curve flattens past this depth
callout pointer — connects a marked point on a curve to its explanatory note; arrow points at the note
highlight / the point — the case where a stackless exception earns its keep
annotation — explanatory note panel
